summary: Create standard troubleshooting playbook for tiered batching (fast/standard/cost-efficient) + common failure modes
description:
Request (from CS/SE): We need a standard troubleshooting playbook for tiered batching (fast/standard/cost-efficient) that Support, Solutions Engineering, and on-call can follow during beta + early GA. Current guidance is scattered across Slack threads, PR descriptions, and dashboards.

Background / why now
- We are seeing repeat questions around:
  1) "I set cost-efficient and now I have more timeouts" (see SUP-18492)
  2) "Tier vs explicit overrides" confusion; customers can’t tell what’s actually applied (see SUP-18510)
- During staged rollout, we need consistent instructions for validating behavior, collecting the right artifacts, and knowing when to recommend opt-out vs escalate.

Deliverable
- A single playbook/checklist that:
  - Defines symptoms and likely causes per tier
  - Lists the minimum data to collect (request IDs, region, model, route, streaming vs non-streaming, prompt length bucket, concurrency estimate)
  - Points to the correct dashboards/metrics and how to interpret them
  - Specifies safe customer workarounds (tier change, specific knob overrides, rate limit tuning) and what NOT to recommend
  - Includes escalation criteria and ownership (Support → SRE → Runtime)

Scope: troubleshooting content to include (MVP)
1) Identify effective configuration
   - How to confirm the effective tier + whether explicit batching knobs override tier defaults.
   - If available, use the "config explain" endpoint/metadata in responses/Console to validate the effective parameters.

2) Common failure modes + first checks
   A) Increased timeouts / p95 blowups after switching to cost-efficient
      - Check queue delay distribution and admission control/load shedding signals.
      - Look for max_queue_delay too high for the customer’s client timeout.
      - Confirm overload protection reason codes and whether cancellation/timeout rates increased.

   B) Streaming cadence regression (fast tier)
      - Validate token cadence and decode prioritization behavior.
      - Confirm streaming route is supported for the tier and look for known regressions.

   C) Unexpected latency variance (standard tier)
      - Identify high variance in prompt length buckets or concurrency; check batch formation histograms.
      - Confirm region/model family defaults; verify no model/GPU-specific override mismatch.

   D) OOM / memory pressure symptoms (usually cost-efficient at high concurrency)
      - Look for KV cache pressure metrics/alerts; confirm compaction thresholds and max batch caps.
      - Identify long-context requests and whether they align with tier guidance.

3) What artifacts to request from customer / internal teams
   - Example request IDs spanning normal + bad behavior
   - Route (chat/completions/embeddings), model, region, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
   - Client timeout settings; retry policy; streaming read timeout
   - Approximate traffic (RPS) and concurrency
   - Whether they changed any explicit batching settings (max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, etc.)

4) Recommended workarounds (approved list)
   - Temporary tier downgrade (cost-efficient → standard) if error/timeout rate increases beyond threshold.
   - For streaming, prefer fast/standard unless SRE confirms queue delay + cadence are within limits.
   - If they must stay on cost-efficient, tighten max_queue_delay_ms to match client timeout budget (only if supported for the deployment) and verify via dashboards.

5) Escalation rubric
   - Escalate to SRE on-call if: p95 latency regression > tier threshold; timeout/cancel rate spike; any 5xx increase.
   - Escalate to Runtime if: reproducible scheduler/tier mapping issue; model-family override bug; suspected KV cache pressure regression.
   - Include links to dashboards, request IDs, and exact tier/override settings in escalation.

Owner(s)
- Primary: DevEx (Alex Martinez) with SRE review (Allison Grant / Rafael Mendes) and Runtime review (Sofia Ivanova or Omar El-Sayed).

Acceptance criteria
- Playbook is published in a stable location (Confluence) and linked in #support and #incidents pins.
- Support can answer: "What tier is actually applied?" and "What do we check first for timeouts?" without engineering assistance.
- Includes a short "quick triage" section (5 minutes) and a deeper "investigation" section (30–60 minutes).

Out of scope (for MVP)
- Full customer-facing doc/FAQ (handled separately by docs site updates)
- Automated diagnostics; this is a human-run playbook.
comments: 2025-03-13 (Miguel Santos): Logging this because we’ve had the same debugging loop twice this week. CS/SE doesn’t have a single source of truth for (a) interpreting queue delay metrics and (b) telling whether explicit overrides are in effect. SUP-18492 and SUP-18510 are representative. Request: one playbook with the approved workaround list + escalation criteria.

2025-03-14 (Alex Martinez): Assigned to DevEx. I’ll draft the playbook but need SRE + Runtime to sanity check thresholds and failure-mode guidance. Specific ask: confirm which metrics are stable/available everywhere during beta (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

2025-03-14 (Allison Grant): For queue delay, please anchor on the definitions in the performance standards page and the tier SLO doc. Also add a note that queue delay can be noisy at low volume—don’t overreact unless it correlates with p95 and timeouts. I can review a draft early next week.

2025-03-15 (Sofia Ivanova): Please include a section explicitly calling out streaming vs non-streaming. Most “it got worse” reports we’ve seen were streaming cadence + decode prioritization interactions or customers using aggressive client timeouts. Also call out that long-context requests can break assumptions for cost-efficient if they’re mixed with short prompts.

2025-03-18 (Alex Martinez): Draft ready for review. Includes quick triage: (1) confirm effective tier (Console/config explain), (2) check p95 + timeout rate, (3) check queue delay + batch size distributions, (4) check overload protection reason codes. Added approved workarounds and escalation template.

2025-03-19 (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed. Added explicit rollback guidance: if timeout rate increases >0.3% absolute (or customer SLO breach), recommend tier revert and open SUP escalation to track. Also added “don’t recommend raising client timeout blindly” note—customers should align it with tier budget.

2025-03-20 (Alex Martinez): Published internal playbook and posted link in #support. Marking resolved. Follow-up: we should add a small snippet to the Console tooltip linking to the playbook once the UI ship is complete.
resolution: Published an internal Tiered Batching Troubleshooting Playbook (quick triage + deep dive), including approved workarounds and escalation criteria. SRE and Runtime reviewed thresholds and metric interpretation guidance. Link shared with CS/SE via #support pins; referenced from SUP-18492/SUP-18510 for consistent handling.
